newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir to have latest problem fixed on Friday - agency.
newsitem.headline: Mir to have latest problem fixed on Friday - agency.

text.p: Russian space chiefs said on Friday they hoped to fix by the end of the day special devices on the damaged Mir space station which keep its solar panels facing the sun to soak up maximum power for the energy-starved craft.

Interfax news agency quoted Mission Control as saying it had established the reason for the failure on Thursday of the so-called gyrodine devices and hoped to have them working again by the end of the day.

Interfax quoted Mission Control as saying one of the devices controlling the gyrodines had failed and the three-man Russian-U.S. crew would have to replace it. This would involve "a large amount of work", it said.

While the devices were out of order, the cosmonauts had to fire their rocket engines to keep Mir lined up to the sun and avoid losing even more electric power. But Mir's fuel resources were limited, the agency said.

The station already lost up to half of its power supply last week after a June 25 collision with an unmanned Progress cargo ship, which also holed one of Mir's scientific modules during a docking exercise.
